short_description: Consumer-facing appearance trait that reports a cautious panel-relative signal for natural light-brown hair tendency within the current local reference panel.
summary_note: Usable consumer-facing appearance trait with practical raw-array support and a clearer interpretation boundary between inherited tendency and current observed hair color for the no-imputation workflow.
what_it_measures: A panel-relative polygenic signal associated with a tendency toward naturally lighter brown hair coloration, calibrated within the current local empirical reference panel.
interpretation_template: Light-brown hair tendency is presented here as a cautious relative appearance signal, not a direct readout of current observed hair color. {interpretation}
caution_text: Use as a cautious panel-relative signal only. No imputation or ancestry-adjusted normalization is used, and the output should not be treated as a deterministic real-world result or as a direct readout of current observed hair color.
limitations: Percentiles and z-scores are relative to the local reference panel, not to a population-wide benchmark.
Observed hair color can also shift with age, graying, dyeing, and other non-genetic factors, so this should not be treated as a deterministic prediction of current hair color.
confidence_note: Confidence reflects overlap and reference robustness under the no-imputation raw-array workflow, not certainty about the real-world trait.
reference_note: Percentiles and z-scores are calibrated against a local empirical reference artifact built from raw-array files in this project; they are panel-relative, not population-wide.
